subject: gov.policy
name: Administration modernisation ministry leadership
milestone: Senior management named across the ministry and its agencies, August 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a recorded appointment
position_end: New senior management has been named across the ministry of modernisation of the administration and the public service, including the director-general of the national e-governance agency; no mandate, programme or budget accompanies the appointments
note: Naming an agency’s leadership is the first thing the base holds about that agency’s current direction.

subject: gov.policy
name: Communication and digital economy portfolio
status: Implemented, held on an interim basis
milestone: Minister dismissed by decree made public 2026-08-21
position_start: A substantive minister of communication, digital economy and innovation in post
position_end: The minister dismissed by presidential decree with no reason given, the ministry's secretary-general appointed interim head, and the portfolio without a substantive holder
note: the employment, labour and social protection minister was dismissed in the same decree; named successors in circulation are publications' own speculation

subject: gov.policy
name: Guinee Digitale 2023-2027, the national digitalisation strategy
milestone: Version 1.2 dated 11 June 2024
position_end: The roadmap records the absence of interoperability between state systems as a standing weakness and programmes the answer as numbered initiatives: mapping existing information systems, an interoperability guide, a data exchange policy, mutualisation of government digital resources, a national interoperability platform and a government enterprise architecture, alongside establishing the data protection authority and formulating an open public data policy. It names ISO 9001, 27001, 20000 and 22301 among its reference standards. It is a plan, not evidence that any framework or platform exists

subject: gov.policy
name: Ministere de la Communication, de l'Economie numerique et de l'Innovation (MCENI)
milestone: Portfolio held unchanged through the reshuffle of 27 July 2026
position_start: Ministere des Postes, Telecommunications et de l'Economie numerique (MPTEN)
position_end: MCENI, merged February 2026, minister unchanged through the July 2026 reshuffle
note: A World Bank tender published the same week still names MPTEN as the supervising department.

subject: gov.policy
name: National Assembly ICT committee
milestone: First working session 2026-08-07
position_end: Constituted and sitting, with mobile money, social-media regulation and network security named as its priorities, to be worked in coordination with the telecommunications ministry
note: the priorities are the committee chair's own statement at its first session; no work programme or timetable is published

subject: gov.policy

milestone: Stakeholder drafting workshop opened 2026-06-19
position_end: A drafting process opened on 19 June 2026, led by the DNTIEN and covering data quality, security, interoperability and responsible use within Vision Simandou 2040; no adoption date is stated

milestone: Pillar 3 launched at Transform Africa Summit 2025, targeting digital at 20% of GDP
position_start: Digital named one of five pillars
position_end: Pillar 3 launched with a 20%-of-GDP target
sources: 2025-11-19 Transform Africa Summit 2025 (Conakry) - Simandou 2040 Pillar 3, TELEMO, SANIA-SADX and the closing wrap

status: Implemented, its stated period now ended

note: The base holds no successor to the strategy for the period after 2025.

subject: gov.policy
name: Study on public data hosting and a sovereign cloud
milestone: Findings presented in Conakry 23 May 2026
position_end: The state digitalisation agency held a restitution session on a World Bank-supported study into the hosting of public data and the development of a sovereign cloud, run with an external consultancy and attended by the digital economy ministry, the cybersecurity agency, the telecommunications regulator, the broadband company, the electricity utility, the central bank and the tax directorate. Discussion covered data centre infrastructure, cybersecurity, resilience of state information systems and cloud governance. It is a study restitution, not an adopted localisation rule: no migration obligation, timetable or legal instrument is reported

subject: gov.legislate
name: ARPT supervision of electronic transactions and mobile money
milestone: Presidential decree of 21 May 2026 added audit, control and certification powers
position_end: In force, and widened: the posts and telecommunications regulator supervises electronic transactions including mobile money, and from May 2026 also audits, controls and certifies the information systems used in them (2026-05)
note: Electronic-commerce providers must hold a .gn or .com domain, a dedicated site and a secured transaction facility, and price in Guinean francs inclusive of taxes and delivery. The 8-page artefact is image-only, so every provision is the agency's summary.

subject: gov.legislate

position_start: Payment systems governed by central bank instructions, conventions and rulebooks rather than by statute (2025-08)
position_end: Payment systems governed by central bank instructions, conventions and rulebooks rather than by statute, covering real-time gross settlement, cheque and bill clearing, Swift and the clearing house
note: The published page is an index of instruments, each behind its own link; the titles are the page's own text and the instruments themselves were not fetched.

position_end: Does not exist

subject: gov.legislate
name: Decree charging the digitalisation agency with inter-administration exchange
milestone: Amending decree D/2023/0232
position_end: The decree amends the 2022 act creating the state digitalisation agency and charges it with harmonising the choice of norms, standards and equipment across state services and with the establishment and management of unified tools of communication, collaboration and exchange within and between administrations, services, institutions and other state bodies at central, deconcentrated and decentralised level. It is the clearest enacted legal basis for inter-administration data exchange. The scan's own decree-number and date fields are blank and the text extraction stops mid-article, so the date is a proxy from the hosting path

subject: gov.legislate
name: Decree on security audit and certification of electronic-transaction systems
milestone: Read on national television, 21 May 2026
position_end: Three-yearly security audits made compulsory for every public and private body carrying on electronic transactions, with certificates of conformity issued by the regulator and compliance duties extended to foreign providers serving Guinean residents
note: The provisions are as reported; the decree itself is not held.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Decrees creating the personal identification number and the persons register
milestone: Three decrees gazetted 14 April 2025
position_end: Three decrees of the same date carry the identity architecture. The first creates an 18-character personal identification number, permanent, univocal and for life, assigned to every citizen on issue of the birth record and to foreigners on entry in the persons register, expressly not proof of nationality, composed of 13 digits, three letters and a two-digit check key over sex, birth year and month, place of birth and a random block. The second constitutes the national register of natural persons as the biographic and biometric database fed by the civil status register, requires the number to be presented when requesting any public or private service, and lists the data captured including digitally captured fingerprints and the parents' numbers. The third sets security, integrity and data-protection conditions for civil-status data

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Analysis and Regulation Platform (PARN)
milestone: Created by the decree of 21 May 2026 to monitor foreign digital services
position_end: Created by decree; not on record as operating

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Compliance Fee (RCN) on foreign digital services
milestone: Decree signed 21 May 2026
position_end: 3% flat rate for twelve months, then 1.5-7% by service category; exemption below 250m GNF of annual taxable revenue
note: 250m GNF is given in the source as roughly US$28,600 (2026-05).

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Sovereignty Fund (FSN)
milestone: Created by the decree of 21 May 2026, financed primarily from the RCN
position_end: Created by decree; no capitalisation, governance or first disbursement published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic signature implementing decree
milestone: Signed by the president 2026-08-19
position_end: A decree fixing the implementing rules for electronic signature under article 1003 of the Civil Code, giving an electronic signature the same probative force as a paper writing where it is authentic, unfalsifiable, non-reusable, unalterable and irrevocable, extending it to administrative, private-sector and person-to-person electronic acts and imposing duties on electronic-certification services
note: no certification authority is yet accredited on the record held

name: Loi L/2015/018/AN on telecommunications and information technologies
milestone: Enacted 2015
position_end: In force as the sector statute for telecommunications and information technologies

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi L/2016/035/AN on electronic transactions
milestone: Adopted 26 July 2016, the date established from the 2021 implementing decree that cites it
position_end: In force as the frame for electronic signature, digital archiving, certification of information systems, consumer information duties in online commerce and the related fraud and forgery offences (2026-08)
note: The agency publishes the law as a 14-page image-only scan with no text layer, so the provisions are its own summary rather than the statute's words.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Payment systems law
milestone: At terms-of-reference stage under WARDIP, awaiting the World Bank's no-objection
position_end: No payments statute
note: Position from the BCRG project register, which is undated; its latest dated entry is 2025-01-28.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Public-administration legal framework consolidation
milestone: Workshop opened on three bills, August 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a consolidated programme
position_end: A workshop has opened to consolidate the legal framework of the public administration around three bills, including a rewritten law on the organisation and functioning of the public service; no text, tabling date or adoption route is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics law and its implementing texts
milestone: Institute's consolidated compendium
position_end: The statistics institute's own compendium reproduces the 2014 law organising and regulating statistical activity together with the 2015 decrees on the national statistics council and on financing of the national statistical programme, and the orders on the council's specialised commissions, on the obligation of administrations and public bodies to transmit data to the national statistical system, and naming council members. The law invokes the principles of objectivity, confidentiality and efficiency. No amendment since 2015 is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Central bank position on crypto-asset trading
milestone: Communiqué issued 2026-08-19
position_end: The central bank states it has granted no licence or authorisation to any entity for crypto-asset trading or online financial placement, sets out seven warning signs of fraudulent offers, notes that registration with a foreign authority is not a domestic licence, and reserves the right to refer illegal fund collection, money laundering and fraud to the courts
note: a warning communiqué rather than a licensing regime; no regulation of virtual assets is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Consumer-protection conditions on NimbaPay
milestone: AGUIDUTEN published twelve conditions on the day after launch; no regulator or operator response on file
position_end: Twelve conditions published; unanswered

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection authority
milestone: Bill in inter-commission at the transition council
position_end: The authority exists in law and not in fact. The 2016 statute provides for its creation by regulation and repeatedly assigns functions to it. On 20 June 2024 the transition council's permanent commissions met in inter-commission with officials from the prime minister's office, the telecommunications and justice ministries and the government secretariat on the bill establishing it; councillors raised concerns over the designation of members, their mandates and the absence of the diaspora, and those observations had to be addressed before plenary examination. Nothing located since shows it was constituted: no appointed members, no organising decree and no website

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law
milestone: Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal-data protection adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by President Alpha Conde; date precision year only, no promulgation date published
position_end: The governing instrument is Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and the protection of personal data, whose text is held from the National Assembly's own publication: it sets definitions, processing principles and data subject rights including erasure, restriction and portability, repeatedly assigns functions to a personal data protection authority to be created by regulation, defines a third country as a non-regional state and makes transfers there subject to prior authorisation. The authority it provides for has never been constituted. The capture stops mid-article, so this is an excerpt of a longer statute
sources: 2016-01-01-guinea-loi-l2016-037-an-cybersecurite-protection-donnees|2025-11-19 Transform Africa Summit 2025 (Conakry) - Simandou 2040 Pillar 3, TELEMO, SANIA-SADX and the closing wrap|2016-07-01-loi-l2016-037-an-cybersecurite-protection-donnees
note: ANSSI publishes the law as a 57-page image-only scan with no text layer, so its provisions are the agency's summary rather than the statute's own words.

subject: gov.protect
name: National cybersecurity and data-protection awareness campaign
milestone: Campaign launched June 2026
position_end: The cybersecurity agency, with World Bank programme support, launched a campaign in two strands: training for magistrates, judges, court officers and judicial police from 15 to 17 June 2026 on cybercrime, digital evidence and chain of custody, and student awareness sessions at two universities on phishing, account protection, digital identity and personal data protection. It is capacity building; it does not create or staff the data protection authority the 2016 law provides for

subject: gov.protect
name: Prosecutions under the cybersecurity and data-protection law
milestone: First conviction on file, 19 August 2026
position_end: A court of first instance convicted an activist, entrepreneur and school founder of insult and defamation by means of a computer system on 19 August 2026, sentencing him to six months' imprisonment of which five are suspended and a 40 million GNF fine, and ordering the deletion of his Facebook account; the conviction rests on article 363 of the penal code and article 29 of the cybersecurity and personal-data protection law. The prosecution had sought a year and argued that a conviction would set an example to other social-media users, and the defence, which had asked for acquittal, said it would consider an appeal
note: the deletion of an account is ordered as a criminal penalty, which the base holds no other instance of

position_end: Ratified domestically on 26 July 2017 by presidential decree taking effect from signature; the African Union's own status list records ratification or accession at 31 July 2018 and deposit at 16 October 2018, and the two dates measure different acts (2026-02)
note: The ratification decree's own Journal Officiel publication is now held (Août 2017 issue, p. 401), alongside the promulgation decree for the authorising law, Décret D/2017/178/PRG/SGG (p. 400 of the same issue; gazette OCR degraded). subject: gov.regional
name: Plateforme des regulateurs de l'audiovisuel of UEMOA states and Guinea (PRA-UEMOA-Guinee)
milestone: 12th General Assembly opened at Conakry 2026-08-31, presidency passing to Guinea
position_start: A standing platform of the eight UEMOA states and Guinea, with the presidency held elsewhere
position_end: The presidency passed to Guinea at the 12th General Assembly in Conakry, whose two-day agenda was harmonising the legal and technical tools for regulating social platforms against cybersecurity and social-cohesion risks, including AI-generated disinformation and deepfakes, and strengthening the standing of regulators over digital platforms
note: no harmonised instrument, timetable or funding is announced; the Justice Minister opened the assembly arguing for a framework that protects without stifling and regulates without censoring, and called cybersecurity a question of sovereignty

milestone: Delegation met the host's IT, cybersecurity, regulatory and digital-service institutions
position_end: A government delegation was among eight from seven African countries hosted by Rwanda's cooperation agency in a single week at the end of August 2026, meeting its IT, cybersecurity, regulatory and digital-service institutions
note: no agreement, programme or replication commitment is recorded, and the account does not say what the delegation concluded

subject: gov.standards
name: Institut Guineen de Normalisation et de Metrologie
milestone: Attributions fixed by presidential decree
position_end: The national standards and quality body is a public administrative establishment with legal personality and financial autonomy, under the technical supervision of the industry ministry and the financial supervision of the finance ministry. Its mandate covers drafting national standards or adopting foreign and international ones, publishing and promoting them, running laboratories, operating the national conformity mark and regional marks, metrological control and calibration certificates, and participating in the national accreditation system. The record is a press transcription of the decree read on national television rather than the gazette text, and the decree number is not given; no catalogue of standards it has issued is held

subject: gov.standards

milestone: Relaunched 2026-08-06
position_end: Sitting again, producing a regular statement of state financial operations against the 2014 international manual, and still facing inconsistent data across the Treasury, the central bank and other agencies

status: Implemented, working referentials rather than binding standards

position_end: The state digitalisation agency publishes four referentials for state information systems: registration of government domains, data security, source code management, and rules of interoperability for information systems. The interoperability referential is the only national interoperability standard located. Its version number and the absence of any adopting decree, order or gazette reference on the page indicate a working technical referential rather than a binding national standard, and the page carries no publication date

subject: gov.standards
name: Statistical quality: national accounts rebasing and the harmonised price index
milestone: April 2026 price bulletin
position_end: The statistics institute, with support from four international institutions, completed a rebasing of national accounts from 2006 to 2018, raising measured output by 51.2 per cent and widening coverage from 34 branches and 54 products to 104 branches and 187 products, bringing in the informal sector, financial services, research and digital activity. Its monthly consumer price bulletin uses the regional harmonised methodology on a 2019 base with national coverage across all eight administrative regions, 5,619 points of sale and 14,522 monthly readings. The methodological note behind the rebasing is not published, and the institute's own national quality assurance framework is not evidenced as adopted

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet and mobile usage
milestone: Ministerial pressure on the leading operator
position_end: The regulator reported 12.8 million mobile subscribers at end-June 2025, 89.1 per cent penetration, and 8.3 million internet subscriptions, about 58 per cent of the population; the international telecommunications union estimates 33.3 per cent internet usage and 82.2 per cent mobile penetration for 2024, with 3G coverage 81.3 per cent and 4G 77 per cent, and a 5 GB mobile data basket at 5.16 per cent of monthly income a head in 2025 against a 2 per cent affordability benchmark. About 6 per cent of neighbourhoods and districts lacked adequate mobile coverage in the second quarter of 2025 and one operator holds 76.2 per cent of the market. Subscription counts overstate unique users because each active card is counted separately

milestone: Represented at the 15th continental peering forum, 17-20 August 2026
position_end: The national internet exchange point's executive secretary represented the country at the fifteenth African peering and interconnection forum in Kigali from 17 to 20 August 2026, supported by the communications, digital economy and innovation ministry through a regional digital integration programme, with the stated aim of strengthening the exchange point's place in the continental interconnection network
note: attendance is what is recorded: no peering agreement, member count, traffic figure or local-traffic share is published for the exchange point itself

position_end: The first loop of the roughly 4,300-4,500 km backbone runs at 400 Gb/s from 20 May 2026, up from 200 Gb/s and from 50 Gb/s in December 2024, with 600 Gb/s across the whole infrastructure targeted by the end of 2026
sources: 2026-05-22-guinee-backbone-capacite-400-gbs-huawei|2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026
note: Ministry-reported figures; no independent measurement on file.

position_end: In force from 28 July 2026, covering Facebook, YouTube and TikTok; still running 2026-08-07; a consumer-protection union additionally reports WhatsApp restricted and bandwidth broadly reduced for several months, with ISPs and mobile operators stating the decision was not theirs (2026-08-04); no authority has acknowledged it

milestone: Operator's own specification
position_end: The only long-standing commercial colocation facility in the country: 228.91 square metres across three rooms, the meet-me room and colocation room linked by two 96-strand fibre cables, serving telecom operators, internet service providers and other customers, with round-the-clock support, three power sources including two 400 kVA generators and battery banks with 72 hours autonomy, precision cooling in redundant mode, gas fire suppression, camera surveillance, badge access control and a gendarmerie post. No tier rating, rack count or information-technology power figure is published, and the page describes this facility only, not national capacity

subject: infra.energy
name: Distribution network rehabilitation
milestone: Early market engagement for the Labe works
position_end: The energy ministry's own performance-contract evaluation of 21 November 2025 sets out the position across the value chain: a dam under construction to add generation, regional interconnection lines already operational, solar plants and mini-grids being developed notably in rural areas, continuing improvement in supply with measures under way to reduce localised faults, and two access projects modernising and extending distribution. It publishes no interruption counts or baseline against which the claimed improvement can be checked. A pre-tender market engagement notice of 15 January 2026 covers rehabilitation, reinforcement and extension of the medium and low-voltage networks of one regional centre and two substations, which is where the utility's own reporting attributes most faults

subject: infra.energy
name: Donkeyah hydroelectric plant
milestone: Commissioned 26 December 2025
position_end: A 17 MW hydroelectric plant at Friguiagbe, built in the 1970s, was commissioned under a public-private partnership between the national utility and a private industrial group, adding 17 MW of hydro capacity and presented as improving service to the surrounding prefecture and the wider network. The record is the utility's promotional post rather than a technical commissioning report: no availability, output or dispatch figure is given

subject: infra.energy
name: Electricity and water supply constraints
milestone: Financier's appraisal-stage document
position_end: National electricity access rose from 18 per cent in 2013 to 53 per cent in 2024, 89 per cent urban against 21 per cent rural. The utility carries losses of 30 per cent and collections of 42 per cent, customer revenue covered 14 per cent of operating costs in 2024, sector subsidies reached USD 317 million or 1.2 per cent of output, and arrears to independent producers exceed USD 1.2 billion. In 2024 low rainfall and a fuel-depot explosion forced emergency thermal leasing and imports, exposing the fragility of a hydro-dependent mix of which only a third of the 6,000 MW potential is exploited; mining demand alone is expected to exceed 700 MW by 2028. On water, 23 per cent of the population had piped access in 2022, 47 per cent urban and 8.1 per cent rural

subject: infra.energy
name: Grid reliability indicators
milestone: 2025 annual report published
position_end: The national utility's 2025 annual report is the only source carrying reliability indicators directly: average interruption duration of 72.1 hours and average interruption frequency of 23 for 2025, alongside energy not distributed, the state of the interconnected and non-interconnected networks, production, transport, losses and commercial performance, and a 2025-2029 strategic plan whose priorities are consolidating production and transport, reducing undelivered energy, improving service quality and accelerating digitalisation. The figures are the operator's own, there being no separate regulator series, and they cover the interconnected and non-interconnected networks rather than a uniformly weighted national index

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural electrification framework and national plan
milestone: Financing round table for the national plan
position_end: The 2013 statute liberalises generation, transmission and distribution in rural and peri-urban areas for installations of 500 kW or less, provides for a rural electrification agency, creates a rural electrification council as the orientation and programming body, and names a rural electrification fund as the source of subsidies, with two project routes, priority projects planned from the national plan and local-initiative projects selected by competitive call. Rural electricity access stands at 25.7 per cent against an exploitable hydroelectric potential put at over 6,000 MW and a government target of universal access by 2040. A financing round table of 25 November 2025 sought blended public, private and partnership mechanisms; it records pledges of intent, not signed agreements, and gives no figure for money committed

subject: infra.capacity
name: Capacity milestones under the regional digital integration programme
milestone: Fourth implementation report, 12.91 per cent disbursed
position_end: The financier's fourth implementation report records recruitment of specialised technical profiles within the state digitalisation agency nearing completion, a memorandum signed with the international telecommunications union to deploy high-impact electronic services and an interoperability platform, a completed cybersecurity feasibility study with public-key infrastructure bidding documents being prepared, procurement for a national incident response team launched but delayed, a digital addressing tender opened in November 2025 with implementation expected mid-2026, and a study tour hosted for a neighbouring country. Its results tables record 101 government officials trained on cybersecurity and data protection against a target of 4,300 by December 2028, and rate institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability as a substantial risk

subject: infra.capacity
name: State digitalisation agency's mandate over government systems
milestone: Created by decree D/2022/0196
position_end: The agency created in April 2022 is the formal locus of state capacity over government systems: aligning technology choices across state services, setting standards, interconnecting all services and institutions through a state intranet, running unified communication and collaboration tools, an integrated financial and administrative management system, dematerialisation and electronic archiving, decision-support and government-monitoring systems, performance indicators for state information systems and evaluation of state investment. Two attributions bear directly on capacity: it holds technical tutelage over all state agents in charge of the State's information systems and is responsible for their training, and it coordinates the operation and management of national and other public data centres. The page states the mandate, not staffing levels or vacancies

subject: infra.capacity
name: Universite Numerique de Guinee (UNG)
milestone: ISFAD converted into UNG by presidential decree, published the evening of 30 July 2026, under Loi L/2023/0016/CNT
position_start: ISFAD (Institut superieur de formation a distance)
position_end: Erected as Universite Numerique de Guinee (UNG), an etablissement public a caractere scientifique with legal personality and an 11-member governing board; mandate covers online higher education, continuing education and digital-pedagogy support
note: Implementation assigned to the ministers of higher education, finance and the public service; no programme, budget or launch date for online offerings published.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: ANSSI (national cybersecurity agency)
milestone: Named as an established agency in the Smart Africa host profile
position_end: Established; no published mandate, budget or reporting on file
sources: 2025-09-09 Get to know The Republic of Guinea Home of Transform Africa Summit 2025
note: No founding instrument for ANSSI is held; the wiki records the agency as page-less (GAP-GIN-001).

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybersecurity statute
milestone: Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal-data protection adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by President Alpha Conde; date precision year only, no promulgation date published
position_end: The cybersecurity statute is Loi L/2016/037/AN, whose text is held from the National Assembly's own publication rather than only through the agency's summary: it reaches cybercrime offences on national territory and offences requiring collection of electronic evidence, and carries the personal data protection regime in the same instrument. The capture stops mid-article, so this is an excerpt
note: ANSSI publishes the law as a 57-page image-only scan with no text layer, so its provisions are the agency's summary rather than the statute's own words.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Global Cybersecurity Index score
milestone: 56.55 of 100 in the 2024 edition
note: The publisher's free tier carries the 2020 and 2024 values only; the five-pillar breakdown and the intervening years are paywalled.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Politique de Securite des Systemes d'Information de l'Etat (PSSIE)
milestone: Validation workshop held 2025-04-18
position_end: Validated in workshop by ANSSI in April 2025, and followed by three decrets of 22 June 2026 on audit, control and certification of information systems and on the certification reference for networks and systems

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Centralised graduate-tracking data platform for technical and vocational education
milestone: Expressions of interest issued 30 September 2025
position_end: An expression-of-interest notice for an international consultancy to build a centralised platform for collection and analysis of data from the computerised graduate-tracking system of technical and vocational education, under a development bank financing, running nine months with a start planned for May 2026. It is the procurement act that commits the country to a consolidated diploma and graduate data layer; no award or platform is recorded

subject: dpi.exchange
name: GovStack interoperability layer (WARDIP)
milestone: Two platforms presented to the prime minister 2026-08-20
position_end: A national e-service portal for dematerialising citizen and business services and a national interoperability portal between existing government systems, both run by the state digitalisation agency, presented to the prime minister with a full service simulation and an inter-ministerial commitment sought; the e-service portal is built as the service component of the single-window project
note: presented rather than launched; no service count, go-live date or connected-agency list is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Guichet Unique du Commerce Exterieur de Guinee (GUCEG)
milestone: Impact 360 forum on the platform, 26 June 2026
position_end: Trade formalities taken online on a platform interconnected with the commercial banks, the central bank, customs, the Port autonome de Conakry and the shipping lines
note: The gains claimed - shorter procedures, lower costs, better secured state revenue - are the platform's director-general's own, with no figure published behind them.

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National interoperability and identity-verification platform (ONECI / NG Tech Innovation)
milestone: Memorandum of understanding signed in Conakry, 24 July 2026
position_end: MoU signed; no value, duration or scope disclosed and the text is not public

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National One Health platform
milestone: Steering committee activated and protocol signed 2026-08-14
position_end: Steering committee activated on 14 August 2026 with the health, higher education, environment and livestock ministries signing a protocol agreement for shared data, joint epidemiological surveillance and coordinated response to zoonotic and environmental risk
note: no platform build, data-sharing rule, custodian or protection standard for the shared health and animal data is stated

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National platform certifying the identity of telecommunications subscribers
milestone: Decree D/2026/0161 of 22 June 2026
position_end: A decree provides for the deployment and operation of a national platform certifying the identity of subscriber-card holders and users of telecommunications services and products. It is the clearest instrument putting a national identity check inside another sector's system. The regulator's page carries only the decree's title, number and date plus links to two companion decrees of the same day; the articles are not reproduced, so the technical architecture is not established and in particular it is not stated whether the platform queries the national persons register

subject: dpi.exchange
name: PISCES X border identification system
milestone: Inaugurated at Conakry AST international airport, 22 November 2024
position_start: In service at the international airport, synchronising traveller data with international watchlist systems (2025-08)
position_end: In service at the international airport, synchronising traveller data with the INTERPOL, IOM MIDAS and United States customs targeting systems
note: A United States embassy donation; the same embassy funded an IOM project, launched September 2024, to install MIDAS terminals at six land crossings.

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Protocol for use of unified social register data
milestone: Protocol signed 27 June 2024
position_end: The economic and social inclusion agency and the social development fund signed a protocol for the agency to use secured data from the unified social register, in order to reach 51,259 indigent households across nine prefectures under a food-shock window. It is the operative instance of social-protection data exchange: bilateral and request-based, not an automated interoperability layer. The protocol text is not published, and the decree creating the register makes partner access conditional on a request plus a protocol of exactly this kind, with technical interoperability arrangements deferred to a technical note

subject: dpi.exchange
name: X-Road national interoperability platform (ANDE)
milestone: Shown to the Prime Minister 2026-08-20
position_end: Run by ANDE to let public information systems communicate so a user need not supply the same information twice, shown to the Prime Minister alongside the national e-service portal and described as in progress rather than in production; an interministerial committee on state digitalisation was announced at the same briefing
note: No decret, arrete or inter-agency protocol establishing the platform was located

subject: dpi.id
name: Biometric civil registry and national ID (ONECI, MOSIP/TECH5)
milestone: Enrolment opened in Sanoyah commune, phase 1 of 2,000 certificates
position_start: No domestic issuance; WURI closed with ~8,000 unique IDs
position_end: Biometric birth certificates and national-ID enrolment running in one commune
sources: 2026-03-04 Guinea Launches Biometric Birth Certificates in Sanoyah in Civil Registry Modernization Push

subject: dpi.id
name: Biometric passport issuance and mobile enrolment
milestone: Mobile enrolment teams deployed from 2026
position_end: The security minister set out the operating arrangement on national television: biometric passport issuance is a mission of his ministry carried out by the national police directorate, and from 2026 applicants in the interior no longer travel to the capital, mobile enrolment teams being deployed where roughly 500 applicants are gathered, doing both enrolment and on-site delivery, starting with the pilgrimage cohort. An appointment-booking system was announced as the next step. It distinguishes the passport line from the identity office's card and civil-status line; no figures, contract or supplier are given

subject: dpi.id
name: Civil-status digitisation rollout
milestone: Regional workshop cycle closed at Kindia
position_end: The territorial administration ministry's budget address reports for 2025 the digitisation of civil status through the identity office, the establishment of the national persons register and the national civil status register, deployment of digital solutions in 28 communes, mobile registration hearings in 375 communes and a biometric census at national scale, alongside a biometric electoral file, 21,732 electoral agents trained and electoral cartography deployed. A regional workshop cycle closed at Kindia in July 2026 coupling dissemination of the two 2023 laws with continued digitisation and indexing of civil-status archives, installing digitisation centres, training agents and putting monitoring and quality control in place. The figures are self-reported and unaudited, and no volume of records digitised is given

subject: dpi.id
name: Customer identification duty on credit institutions
milestone: Central bank instruction on internal control
position_end: The central bank's instruction on internal control, taken under the banking law, requires regulated credit institutions to identify and verify their customers, with the anti-money-laundering section carrying customer identification, beneficial-owner verification and record retention. It is the closest thing to a standing identity-verification obligation actually in force: there is no evidenced national electronic identity authentication service, no public key infrastructure or trust list, and the electronic-transactions statute is published by the regulator only as a title with no text. It is sectoral and pre-digital, governing identity checks inside the financial sector rather than authentication against the persons register

subject: dpi.id
name: Free issuance of biometric civil-registration documents
milestone: State contractor MGG alleged unprovided-for fees and pay-for-priority at enrolment centres
position_end: Decreed free; fees alleged to be taken at enrolment centres, no ministerial response on file

subject: dpi.id
name: FUGAS biometric civil-service payroll
milestone: Biometric audit confirmed ~130,000 of ~277,000 registered civil servants
position_start: In use since 2024; no audit result published
position_end: 233bn GNF (~US$26.9m, 2025-11) reported saved since 2024
sources: 2025-11-30 Guinea Claims $26.9M Saved Since 2024 with Biometric Audit of Public Workforce (FUGAS)

subject: dpi.id
name: Reallocation of residence-certificate issuance to civil-status officers
milestone: Handover ceremony at the capital governorate
position_end: The elections directorate and the identity office handed residence certificates and habitation attestations to commune secretaries-general and delegated civil-status officers. The residence certificate is henceforth issued free of charge and exclusively by commune secretaries-general, ending the involvement of neighbourhood chiefs, who retain the habitation attestation; the identity office attributes the reform to a convention with the elections directorate and to the two 2023 civil-status laws. A commune secretary-general notes that no residence certificate can issue without a prior habitation attestation from the neighbourhood chief. The convention and any implementing order are not published

subject: dpi.id
name: Unique personal identification number
milestone: Stated as being put in place by the territorial administration minister 2026-08-10
position_end: The territorial administration minister states a unique personal identification number is being put in place alongside digitalisation of the civil-status system; no instrument, issuing authority, number format or enrolment figure is on record
sources: 2025-11-30 Guinea Claims $26.9M Saved Since 2024 with Biometric Audit of Public Workforce (FUGAS)|2026-08-11-guinee-decentralisation-etat-civil-npi
note: a ministerial statement made at a commemorative event, not an instrument

subject: dpi.id
name: WURI-Guinea foundational ID project
milestone: Closed 28 June 2024, two years early, with ~8,000 unique IDs issued
position_end: Closed
sources: 2025-05-02 WURI Implementation Status Report - Cote d'Ivoire and Guinea (P161329 Seq 11)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Adults with a financial account
milestone: Central bank governor's figure, given at the NimbaPay launch
position_end: Close to 36% of adults held a financial account in 2024, up from 4% in 2011, on the central bank governor's account, the rise attributed to electronic money
note: A separate December 2025 account puts adults banked at ~23%; the two use different definitions and have not been reconciled.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cash share of payments at electronically equipped merchants
milestone: Stated by the BCRG's director-general of financial-institution supervision
position_end: More than 70% still in cash (2026-07-23)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Digitisation of pension payment
milestone: December 2025 run named only digital channels
position_end: From July 2025 the social security fund ends cash payment of retirement, survivor and invalidity pensions in favour of bank transfer, mobile wallets and rechargeable cards, with a nationwide information and assistance campaign to migrate pensioners without interruption. Its communique of 22 December 2025, bringing the January instalment forward, names the usual means of collection as bank transfer and mobile telephony only, with no cash option listed: the first communique found that treats digital channels as the sole route for a national pension run. No share of pensions already paid digitally, and no number of pensioners, is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: ECOWAS EPSS integrated payment project
milestone: Withdrawn from the BCRG's 2025 strategic priorities after a single evaluation meeting on 10 July 2024
position_start: Withdrawn from the BCRG's strategic priorities
position_end: Withdrawn from the BCRG's strategic priorities; no visibility on next steps

subject: dpi.pay
name: Licensed electronic-money institutions
milestone: 11 licensed, reported at the BCRG's anti-cash presentation
sources: 2025-11-07 Guinea Plans Mobile Payment System to Ease Cash Shortage

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile financial services subscribers
milestone: 3.2 million at end-June 2025 on the regulator's count
position_end: 3.2 million, of which Orange holds 92 per cent and MTN 8 per cent (June 2025)
note: The regulator's figures as reported; on the same account transactions rose from 540 million in 2021 to 1.44 billion in 2024.

subject: dpi.pay
name: National payment switch
milestone: BCRG-AfricaNenda memorandum signed 5 December 2024 with Guineenne de Monetique
position_end: Not operational as a separate switch

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Payment Systems and Instruments Strategy 2027-2030
milestone: Drafting consultancy advertised 2026-08-14, applications close 2026-08-31
position_end: Out to consultancy as a four-month drafting assignment; no strategy text, budget or adoption date exists
note: advertised by the central bank with a continental payments foundation

subject: dpi.pay
name: NimbaPay national instant payment system
milestone: Officially launched 2026-07-22 under the Prime Minister's patronage
position_end: Live and interoperable: any user can send and receive money instantly between a bank, a microfinance institution and an electronic-money establishment, operated by the Guineenne de la Monetique under the central bank. The governor named digitisation of state payments and cross-border flows as the next steps
note: Built in 127 days on Mojaloop by Guineenne de Monetique, with AfricaNenda and Thitsa Works.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Orange Money bank-account linking service (Acces a ma banque)
milestone: BCI became the seventeenth connected bank, 18 December 2025
position_end: Seventeen banks connected, with balance enquiry, mini-statement and transfers in both directions between a bank account and an Orange Money wallet
note: Linking a bank account to a wallet requires a visit to a branch.

subject: dpi.pay
name: PAPSS participation
milestone: Participant status with no transaction yet recorded on the platform
position_end: Participant, no transaction recorded

subject: dpi.pay
name: Resilient SWIFT infrastructure (BCRG)
milestone: International tender launched for a resilient SWIFT infrastructure at the BCRG; bids due 31 August 2026
position_end: International tender open (BCRG/DGASJ/DSJO/2026), single lot, financed from the BCRG's own resources under its 2026 budget programme; bids due 31 August 2026
note: Submission deadline and public opening date are handwritten on the printed notice and did not survive capture there; a press account gives 31 August 2026 as the deadline.

subject: dpi.pay
name: RTGS migration to ISO 20022
milestone: Second equipment lot delivered 28 January 2025; migration not made
position_start: Launched 2024-06-03, equipment on order, not migrated
position_end: Not migrated; held by unpaid invoices to the supplier CMA and prolonged customs clearance
note: Position stated in the BCRG project register, which is undated; its latest dated entry is 2025-01-28.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Tresor Pay public-payments gateway
milestone: Launched 22 December 2025
position_end: In service for payment of state administrative fees by mobile
sources: 2025-12-23 Guinea rolls out Tresor Pay as digital gateway for public payments

subject: dpi.pay
name: Unique bank identifier and interoperability project (UBI/IN)
milestone: Launched 26 June 2024; reached consultant recruitment
position_end: At consultant recruitment
note: AfDB-financed; position from the undated BCRG register, content vintage early 2025.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Address register
milestone: Street addressing dropped in most communes
position_end: There is no national address register, only a partial municipal street-addressing arrangement in the capital built under successive urban projects. The completion report records the indicator for municipalities with street addressing in place and operational at 3 against an original target of 6 revised down to 3, and states that street addressing was dropped in all communes of the capital except three, along with the parallel fiscal-register work. The project unit worked with the tax directorate on the programme, so the address file was a tax-base instrument rather than a civic addressing utility. The document fixes the historical position; a national digital addressing tender opened in November 2025 under the regional digital programme

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration rate
milestone: Given by the territorial administration minister 2026-08-10
position_end: 72% of births registered (2025)
note: the minister’s own figures, given in a ceremonial statement; no statistical source is named

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land cadastre digitalisation
milestone: First implementation phase agreed 2025-10-12
position_end: A first phase of the Systeme d'Information Foncier covering Conakry and thirteen other towns was set with Geo Consult International, on five pillars — high-resolution aerial imagery, a structured parcel plan for Conakry, a multi-actor land survey, the system itself, and the supporting infrastructure and training; financing for a national phase was under discussion with the Islamic Development Bank

subject: dpi.registry
name: Loi L/2023/0020 on civil status
milestone: Implementing texts worked through in Kindia workshop, January 2026
position_end: In force since 25 October 2023, with implementing texts on civil status and identification worked through in a Kindia workshop in January 2026 and popularised by ONECI from February 2026

subject: dpi.registry
name: Permanent biometric electoral file
milestone: 6.95m electors and 23,681 stations set for the 31 May 2026 coupled elections
position_end: 6.95m electors, 23,681 stations (2026-04)

subject: dpi.registry
name: PN-RAVEC administrative census
milestone: Secured civil-registry inputs delivered to RGPH-4 and the RNPP
position_end: Feeding the RNPP, the electoral roll's single official source

subject: dpi.registry
name: Registre national des personnes physiques (RNPP)
milestone: DGE-ONECI convention institutionalised RNPP-to-roll data sharing
position_start: Not the official source for the electoral roll
position_end: Single official source for the permanent biometric electoral file

subject: dpi.registry
name: Registre Social Unifie (RSU)
milestone: First public coverage figure presented 8 July 2026
position_end: Created by decree of 13 October 2024 within the social development and indigence fund as an information system to identify, register and follow up households potentially eligible for social protection programmes, holding secured biometric data, socio-economic data and a randomly generated unique identification number carrying no geographic or personal information, revised in full every three years, and made the single entry point on which partners' interventions must be based, with interoperability and data access governed by protocol. The first public coverage figure, presented on 8 July 2026, is 977,610 households and 4,860,075 individuals, broken down by region; the report was still circulating for comment and a companion account of the same workshop gives 4,624,633 individuals, so the individual total is not settled while the household count and regional breakdown agree

subject: dpi.registry
name: RETSSM movable-collateral electronic registry
milestone: Rescue consultancy tendered under WARDIP, opening 27 July and closing 17 August 2026
position_end: Software built; institutional, legal and regulatory provisions, security posture and user base not in place

subject: dpi.registry
name: Secured paper supply for digital birth certificates
milestone: Printing stopped for about two weeks
position_end: A nationwide stockout of the secure paper digital birth certificates are printed on has stopped printing for about two weeks: registration continues but no certificate can be issued, and the delegated civil-registry officer for one Conakry commune expects resupply within about a week. Separately, the relocation of the data centre previously hosted at the Maison centrale has disturbed the digital system while engineers reinstall it at a new site
note: the base has now held a secure-paper shortage twice in a month, so a consumable supply chain is the constraint on a digitised register; no procurement, stock level or affected-applicant count is published, and moving the data centre at the same time compounded it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register
milestone: Published extract of fiscally active taxpayers
position_end: The tax directorate's published extract of fiscally active taxpayers is the only public artefact showing the structure of the register: one row per taxpayer with the permanent tax identification number, the older number, the business name, the managing section and the activity code, and it shows the coexistence of the two numbering schemes, rows with a blank legacy number and an unidentified management category. It is an extract rather than the whole register, six years old, and the row count is not a national taxpayer count; the directorate has since migrated to a second-generation core system

subject: dpi.mis
name: Ayooka blood-supply coordination platform
milestone: Founded 2022, described 2026-08-17
position_end: Operating from Guinea as a platform coordinating blood donation and blood-bank logistics across West Africa, founded in 2022 to close coordination gaps between collection centres, blood banks and health facilities and to stop units expiring at one facility while another is short
note: a private platform; no facility count, transfer volume, ministry relationship or health-data protection arrangement is stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Direction Nationale des Domaines et du Cadastre
milestone: Attributions fixed by order of 11 August 2004
position_end: The constitutive instrument of the body that holds cadastral and land-administration data. It establishes the directorate as a national directorate of central administration and gives it the mission of drawing up the national land framing plan, supporting local authorities in setting up and updating communal land plans, drawing up subdivision plans and parcel coding, inventorying land resources and recording them on cartographic bases, census and registration of State and local-authority property with maintenance of the general table of State property, mortgage inscriptions, participation in geodetic networks and production of rental-price statistics. It does not create a digital cadastre: no decree founding a national land information system was reachable

subject: dpi.mis
name: SAFIG tax administration system and the e-Tax portal
milestone: SAFIG2 presented to the CREDAF conference, June 2026
position_end: The e-Tax portal has taken online tax payment since October 2020, and the tax directorate published a performance analysis of SAFIG covering 2020 to September 2025 and presented its successor SAFIG2 to the 39th CREDAF conference in June 2026

subject: dpi.mis
name: School information systems and the national school map
milestone: National school map launched 2026-04-29
position_end: The education ministry's SIGE informatisation programme runs alongside digital registration of primary pupils from February 2026, university registration of the 2025 baccalaureate cohort through SIGU, and a national school map launched in April 2026

subject: dpi.mis
name: SNIS health information system interoperability
milestone: Five facilities interoperating 2026-08-26
position_end: five health facilities in the Mamou and Dalaba districts running a hospital information system with interoperability to the national health platform, with the Dalaba prefectural hospital reporting consultations up
sources: 2026-08-26-lepandaguinee-guinee-a-mamou-et-dalaba-le-pari-de|2025-11-27 Interoperability - key workshop to modernize Guinea's health information system
note: SNIS has no entity page in the wiki (GAP-GIN-002).

subject: dpi.mis
name: Visa Medical hospital digitisation
milestone: Expansion beyond Guinea announced 2026-08-13
position_end: Deployed in 19 Guinean hospitals with more than a million users on a self-financed model, and being extended to Chad, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Morocco
note: a private academy's own figures; no ministry acknowledgement, patient-data protection arrangement or interoperability with the national health information system is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Civil-service housing registration platform
milestone: Opened by ministerial communique 24 August 2026
position_end: The ministry of administrative modernisation and the public service opened an online registration platform for a civil-service social-housing programme, in a communique of 24 August 2026 directing officials to use the official platform alone to complete an interest survey and to read the eligibility conditions and criteria, and warning that no registration, fee or intervention made outside the officially announced arrangement engages the government's responsibility
note: the warning against payments outside the platform is the notable part: it names the fraud the platform is meant to displace

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Criminal-investigation biometric identification system
milestone: Deployed for the police technique et scientifique in Conakry
position_start: Fingerprint identification automated in Conakry, with regional stations submitting material on paper (2025-08)
position_end: Fingerprint identification automated for the one forensic department in the country, with regional stations submitting material on paper
note: The supplier's own case study; it puts the criminal fingerprint database before deployment at 7,500 records.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: E-FONIJ youth insertion platform
milestone: Launched 2026-09-03
position_end: A national platform for youth information, orientation, training, support and job placement, live on the web and on one mobile app store with the other to follow, launched with a national call for partners (2026-09)
note: no user count, vacancy volume, placement figure or funding arrangement is published, and the launch reaches the base through the fund's own communique

subject: dpi.govtech
name: eCNSS online social contributions
milestone: Launched, carrying ~60% of contribution receipts
position_end: In service, ~60% of receipts

subject: dpi.govtech
name: GEDA decrees and orders management tool
milestone: Presidential oversight announced 2026-08-14
position_end: In use for managing decrees and orders, with the President stating on 14 August 2026 that he will personally oversee it to speed administrative processing, tied to accelerating the Simandou 2040 programme
note: no throughput figure, custodian or publication rule is stated, and personal oversight by the head of state is not an institutional control

subject: dpi.govtech
name: GEME state mission-order system
milestone: Launched 2026-08-13
position_end: Launched as an electronic system for managing state mission orders, to control costs and improve accountability, within the administration-modernisation programme
note: no custodian, coverage, cost baseline or saving target is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Guichet Unique des Services Publics (GUSP)
milestone: Guinea-Azerbaijan partnership agreed to build it on the ASAN model
position_end: Partnership agreed; no launch date published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Journal Officiel numerique
milestone: Free online legal gazette carrying 1,100+ journals and 6,000+ texts
position_end: Online and free to access
note: An acquisition attempt on 2026-08-08 found the Secretariat general du gouvernement's Journal Officiel index carrying issues only to April 2025.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: LANDAYA industrial-permits platform
milestone: Industrial licences issued in 72 hours; successor to PLAGED
position_end: LANDAYA in service, 72-hour licence issuance

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National vehicle-attestation platform
milestone: Contract awarded to SIIN and DIGITECH of Cote d'Ivoire
position_end: Contract awarded; no service date published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Nine-project public-administration package
milestone: Nine projects announced, May 2026
position_end: Nine projects announced: GUSP, HR systems, Gouv-Lab, e-Tax, IT inventory, digital skills and FUGAS

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Oeil du Tresor fund-call platform
milestone: Regional training for prefectural treasurers begun in Guinee forestiere
position_end: Rolling out to prefectural treasurers; no cost, vendor or completion date disclosed

subject: dpi.govtech
name: ParcourSup Guinee higher-education admissions portal
milestone: Institutions and programmes published on the portal
position_start: In service for admission to the higher-education system (2025-08)
position_end: In service, carrying six universities, ten higher institutes and one higher school alongside private institutions and their programmes

subject: dpi.govtech
name: TELEMO e-procurement platform
milestone: Dematerialisation rules for public procurement fixed by decree 2026-08-21
position_start: Unveiled at Transform Africa Summit, November 2025
position_end: Launched and digitising the full public-procurement cycle, with a presidential decree of 21 August fixing the rules for dematerialising procurement procedures under article 56 of the 2019 procurement code: a national electronic platform for public contracts and public-private partnerships managed by the finance ministry, mandatory registration of contracting authorities and bidders, and encrypted bid submission. The anti-corruption agency presented it, alongside the mining cadastre, to the United Nations convention review group at Vienna on 4 September 2026 as evidence of transparency reform (2026-09)
