note: a joint government mission went to Kigali in August 2026 for talks whose agenda covered the platform's evolution; the decree does not state whether the national platform is this one or a successor

subject: digital.localgov
name: Local governance support project financing
milestone: Mid-term review launched 2 June 2026
position_start: An earlier local governance project closed on 31 January 2025 (2025-01)
position_end: An 81 million dollar operation run since October 2023 to 30 June 2028, covering all 362 communes under the national vision, whose first component explicitly includes digitalisation of communal accounting through two named software packages and the deployment of communal receivers, while a further component uses a monitoring platform and another deploys participatory budgeting in 375 communes. Performance-based conditions account for 45 per cent of the budget, released against results verified by an independent auditor. The mid-term review opened on 2 June 2026 and reports no findings or coverage figures

subject: digital.localgov
name: Prefectural treasury connection to central systems
milestone: Training under Oeil du Tresor begun in five prefectures of Guinee forestiere
position_end: Yomou, Lola, Beyla, Macenta and N'Zerekore in training

subject: digital.rural
name: Agriculteurs Connectes de Guinee
milestone: First cohort launched at Conakry 2026-08-06
position_end: A first cohort running, pairing a private agritech's field sensors, weather alerts and agronomic advice with the state rural bank's network of over 1,000 service points
note: a private partnership with a state-owned bank rather than a public programme; no cohort size, cost or coverage is stated

subject: digital.rural
name: Clinic+O rural primary-healthcare platform
milestone: Running from November 2025 to December 2026
position_end: Community health workers equipped with tablets and portable diagnostic devices screening for non-communicable diseases in rural health centres
note: Foundation-funded and awarded a 2026 resilience award; no facility count, ministry relationship or health-data protection arrangement is stated.

subject: digital.rural
name: Computer and solar kits for local authority accounting (PANAFIC)
milestone: Contracts awarded 2025-10-01
position_start: No rural connectivity or rural digital-services programme held
position_end: ANAFIC awarded two lots under AFD C2D financing on 1 October 2025: computer kits for 21 local authorities at GNF 836,500,000 and solar kits for seven new rural communes of the interior at GNF 781,060,000, both procured to run the commune accounting and financial management software — the hardware and off-grid power that put it into rural town halls

subject: tech.ai
name: Artificial intelligence in the administration
milestone: Regulator trains four cadres on data and AI
position_end: No instrument governing or deploying artificial intelligence inside the administration was reachable, and no ministerial chatbot, predictive model or automated administrative decision could be identified. The digital platforms the state runs are described by their own official sources as digital and automated, not as artificial intelligence. What is dated is preparation to regulate rather than use: the telecommunications regulator sent four senior staff, including its director of information systems, its legal director, its director of regulation and a cybersecurity engineer, to a regional session on big data analysis and artificial intelligence covering data processing, confidentiality, ethics and the development of sector policy and regulatory frameworks

subject: tech.ai
name: Commitment to put artificial intelligence in the education management system
milestone: Concept-stage document, board approval June 2026
position_end: A US$131.30 million education and skills operation carries a component on strengthening education and skills systems management that will support data-driven governance through an enhanced management information system, monitoring and planning, and will introduce weather event early warning systems using artificial intelligence and analytics, alongside teacher recruitment and deployment policy, formula-based school grant delivery and digital administration platforms. The same paragraph names the problem it answers: management hindered by fragmented ministerial responsibilities, low levels of digitalisation and limited use of data. It is a commitment in an approved and budgeted operation, not evidence of a model in production

subject: tech.ai
name: Cybersecurity agency alert on manipulated media
milestone: Alert issued 12 September 2025
position_end: The cybersecurity agency issued an alert against the manipulation and illicit circulation of artificial-intelligence-generated images and videos targeting public figures including the head of state, nine days before a constitutional referendum. It is the first statement mapping such content onto the existing statute book: the agency asserts civil and criminal liability including takedown and compensation, penalties of five to ten years' imprisonment with heavy fines, and protection of privacy, honour and dignity as fundamental principles, and says it has the technical means to trace online activity and pursue offenders. It applies existing law rather than announcing a new instrument, and the primary alert was posted to a social network whose text was not retrievable

subject: tech.ai
name: DouIA programme and Manifesto of Conakry
milestone: DouIA1 closed and DouIA2 launched with the signing of the Manifesto of Conakry
position_end: DouIA2 launched; no published workplan or budget
note: The only account on file is from a PR-wire outlet; no primary document is held.

subject: tech.ai
name: Dynamic selectivity in the customs system
milestone: Deployed at the port in April 2021
position_end: The customs programme and the national customs service built a dynamic selectivity mechanism that calculates the risk of fraud for each declaration from historical data, deployed at the main port in April 2021, with a simplified interface for creating and updating selectivity criteria and analytical reports generated automatically to assess criteria efficiency. In the first quarter of 2022, 78 per cent of declarations were selected through dynamic selectivity against 12.5 per cent previously, and 93 per cent of declarations the system identified were found non-conforming by officers. The compendium describes risk scoring from historical data, and the machine-learning label attaches to the product line rather than being asserted of this installation

subject: tech.ai
name: Guinea-Rwanda cooperation in AI and e-health
milestone: Areas identified at a Conakry meeting on 20 July 2026; nothing signed
position_end: AI, e-health, e-commerce and electronic invoicing identified for exploration

subject: tech.ai
name: HAC prohibition on AI-generated media content
milestone: Prohibition issued 2025-11-28
position_end: The broadcasting regulator has prohibited media outlets from carrying AI-generated content

subject: tech.ai
name: National AI roadmap 2026-2035
milestone: Validated 2025-12-20 after a UNDP workshop
position_start: No roadmap document, validation date or adopting instrument held
position_end: Validated in three phases — institutional, regulatory and technical foundations; progressive integration of AI into public services; then regional positioning on responsible use — built on an AI Landscape Assessment diagnostic the ministry says makes Guinea the first francophone country to adopt the AILA methodology
note: The roadmap's own text was not reachable, so its legal status and indicators cannot be read off the instrument

subject: tech.ai
name: Six-country Francophone West African AI governance framework
milestone: Adopted and announced 6 July 2026; submitted to the UN Global AI Dialogue
position_end: Adopted by Benin, Burkina Faso, Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea, Mali and Senegal

subject: tech.industry
name: Cauridor cross-border payments infrastructure
milestone: Appointed a chief operating officer; operating in 36 countries
position_end: Guinea-founded, operating in 36 countries (2026-04)

subject: tech.innovate
name: Global Innovation Index rank
milestone: 133rd of 139 economies in the 2025 edition
position_end: 133rd of 139 economies, 27th of 32 in sub-Saharan Africa and 35th of 37 lower-middle-income economies (2025 edition)
note: The 2024 edition carries no ranking for Guinea and the field ranked grew between editions; the publisher puts the 2025 confidence interval at ranks 127 to 136.

subject: tech.innovate
name: Innovation hubs in the AfriLabs directory
milestone: Three Guinean organisations listed
movement: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
position_end: Three organisations listed - an innovation centre, a digital-education hub and a technology incubator (2025)

subject: tech.innovate
name: Startup law and the innovation-support layer
milestone: Draft startup law read through in ministerial session 2025-04-29
position_start: No startup act, innovation fund or incubation programme held
position_end: The startup law is a draft and not an act: a relecture session chaired by the commerce ministry on 29 April 2025 set its objects as an adapted legal and fiscal environment, better access to finance and public-private partnerships, and no promulgated act or Journal Officiel publication is held. Around it sit a startup alliance founded in October 2025, the SabouTech incubator, and a national innovation strategy put out to tender in August 2026

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Distance-training platform for state cadres
milestone: Launched with a ministerial collaboration platform
position_end: The government secretariat's distance-training platform for state cadres was launched alongside a ministerial collaboration platform in April 2024. It was tested and approved by national trainers in seminars for government members, secretaries-general, chiefs of staff and establishment directors, it works without an internet connection so as to reach remote regions, and the head of government required every state cadre to be given measurable and monitored training or self-training objectives. It establishes the delivery system and the training expectation, not any measured level of civil-service digital literacy: no national figure was located

subject: capacity.literacy
name: FabLabs Solidaires network
milestone: Fourth FabLab inaugurated at Coyah 2026-06-03
position_start: No digital-literacy programme or measurement held
position_end: Four labs since 2022 — the Orange Digital Center de Ratoma, the Ecole Nationale des Postes et Telecommunications at Kipe and the SankuLab de Bellevue in Conakry, and from June 2026 the Ecole Regionale des Arts et Metiers at Coyah, the first outside the capital — targeting training for more than 125 women in green trades and digital technologies. No national measurement of digital literacy is held
note: A programme count, not a literacy rate; the measurement half of this question is still unanswered

subject: capacity.training
name: Holberton Guinee software-engineering campus
milestone: Conakry campus launched 16 July 2026
position_end: Operating

subject: capacity.training
name: People trained in digital skills
milestone: 10,000+ reported in the 2025 sector review
position_end: 10,000+ trained, ministry-reported (2026-01)
sources: 2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026

subject: capacity.research
name: Institut Ouest-Africain de Mathematiques, Universite Gamal Abdel Nasser
milestone: Pilot cohort of 45 students teaching ahead of the official opening
position_start: No public research programme, university research centre mandate or published output held
position_end: Structured inside the Universite Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry with two associate lecturers recruited from Benin and Senegal and a pilot cohort of 45 Guinean and foreign students already teaching before the official opening

subject: include.access
name: Digital access for persons with disabilities
milestone: Accessibility upgrade to a civil-society platform
position_end: Two dated movements, neither of them a government service. A regional commission mission and a two-day workshop set implementation terms for the third phase of an assistive-devices programme covering three countries with USD 300,000 committed, in which the national federation of persons with disabilities lists specialised tablets alongside prostheses, wheelchairs, adapted tricycles, hearing aids and white canes; the commission's own officer names the binding constraint as data, persons with disabilities remaining too often invisible in statistics and public policy. A bloggers' association launched an accessibility upgrade to its youth platform in July 2026 adding subtitling, national sign language, audio description, high contrast and zoom, with 24 audiovisual contents produced in French and local languages, designed with an association for deaf young people and tested with the intended users. No accessibility conformance is stated for any public digital service

subject: include.access
name: Gender gap in device ownership and access
milestone: Survey dispatch published August 2024
position_end: The clearest published sex-disaggregated figures are a survey organisation's: men out-own women on mobile phones 96 per cent to 86 per cent and on computers 11 per cent to 7 per cent, with bank accounts at 13 per cent to 8 per cent. It sets these against a female literacy rate of 22 per cent versus 43.6 per cent for men and records that 57 per cent of women have no formal education against 43 per cent of men, which is the mechanism behind the access gap. Fieldwork was face-to-face with 1,200 adults in August 2022. The questions measure personal ownership rather than internet use, and no national sex-disaggregated internet-use series is published

subject: include.access
name: Private electronic-money and wallet market
milestone: CORIS Money (February 2026), Orange Money-BNG interoperability (March 2026) and KS-Wallet (April 2026) entered service
position_end: 11 licensed institutions and three new services, including wallet-to-bank interoperability

subject: include.access
name: Refugee documentation and digital service access
milestone: Institutional appropriation workshop for the refugee commission
position_end: The 2018 asylum statute, described as one of the most comprehensive in West Africa, defines management of refugees and asylum seekers and provides for access to biometric documents, refugee identity cards and travel documents. The load-bearing finding is that although government experts validated the implementing texts in June 2021, no implementing decree has been published, so the biometric documentation entitlement is not operative; on internally displaced people the country is party to the regional convention but has no national legal framework. The refugee commission's executive secretary states its mandate covers registration of asylum seekers, support to status determination, coordination of international protection and integration. Population figures conflict: the ministry publishes over 3,023 refugees and over 3,053 asylum seekers, the refugee agency 2,171 and 172

subject: include.divides
name: Mobile internet cost
milestone: Reported down 25% in the 2025 sector review
position_end: Down 25% over 2025, ministry-reported (2026-01)
sources: 2026-01-14 Guinea Reviews 2025 Digital Sector Gains, Targets Faster Rollout in 2026

subject: data.statistics
name: National strategy for the development of statistics
milestone: Living-conditions survey collection launched
position_end: The national statistics council adopted the second strategy for 2016-2020 as the reference framework for all actors in the statistical field, with four strategic axes, eleven operational objectives, a diagnostic and an action plan costed at 444.2 billion in national currency. No final adopted text of the third-generation strategy for 2021-2025 is published: the institute published a validation workshop in May 2022 and a mid-term update in December 2024, and the international partnership records the country as implementing and due for end evaluation. What is dated is donor-financed execution of the programme in the absence of a published successor: collection for the first wave of the second harmonised living-conditions survey was launched in November 2025 with 108 enumerators covering 4,140 households over three months

subject: data.statistics
name: RGPH-4 population census
milestone: Population of 17,521,167 carried into the electoral file
position_end: Population 17,521,167

subject: data.open
name: External fiscal transparency assessment, 2026
milestone: Country-specific assessment held in full
position_end: The country-specific assessment behind the 2026 fiscal transparency report, held in full
note: a foreign government's assessment on its own criteria; it is the only recurring transparency measure the base holds for this country

subject: data.open
name: Extractive industries transparency validation
milestone: Board decision of 12 May 2026
position_end: The board scored the country 73.5 out of 100 overall against the 2023 standard, with data accessibility and open data scored 90 out of 100, the highest band reached on any transparency-facing requirement, alongside 90 for the licence register, contracts and licences, and production and export data. Against that, civil society engagement scored 50, beneficial ownership 50 and licence allocations 50, and the report records that administrative and procedural rules on civil society organisations produced tangible restrictions on those substantially engaged in implementation. The score covers extractives disclosure only, not government open data generally

subject: data.open
name: Loi L/2020/0027/AN on access to public information
milestone: Published by the National Assembly 2020-12-19
position_start: No open-data portal, policy or re-use instrument held
position_end: Article 10 imposes proactive publication, refreshed at least quarterly, of sixteen categories including statistical, economic and social information, budget and public-finance data at central, regional and local level, national accounts, public debt and procurement projects; Chapitre 3 makes re-use of public information free of charge by default, with cost-recovery fees only for commercial re-use. No national open-data portal is held
note: The statute is held and no portal implementing it is

subject: data.open
name: Statistics institute's open data platform and standards migration
milestone: Migration workshop to the second platform version
position_end: The statistics institute ran a national capacity-building workshop with African Development Bank support on statistical data exchange modelling and migration to the second version of its open data platform, covering population, health, energy, education, industry, prices, external trade, tourism, transport, employment and agriculture, with 22 institute staff and two from the space agency. It is capacity building toward a platform, not an adopted open data policy: the strategy's own initiative to formulate one has not produced an instrument

subject: data.satellite
name: Meteorological use of satellite and observation data (ANM)
milestone: CREWS Accelerated Support Window project closed October 2025
position_start: No earth-observation or satellite data programme held
position_end: A US$250,000 CREWS project rebuilt the national meteorological service after the December 2023 Conakry fuel-depot explosion: a website carrying WIS2box and a CAP composer, 113 warning bulletins published in CAP format, 28 stations revised and connected to the WMO Information System, and Guinea the first African country onboarded by Google Public Alert

subject: geopol.usa
name: Taxation of United States digital-service providers
milestone: Decree of 21 May 2026 brings streaming, cloud, SaaS, advertising and e-commerce into charge
position_end: In charge, with a 90-day requirement to appoint a local representative

subject: geopol.china
name: Huawei in the national digital estate
milestone: Ministerial talks in China 2026-07-03 on a comprehensive memorandum
position_start: No Guinea-specific Chinese digital financing agreement, contract or memorandum held
position_end: Huawei designed and built the roughly 4,300-4,500 km national fibre backbone and remains its technical partner: the first loop went from 200 to 400 Gb/s on 20 May 2026, the second upgrade in eighteen months, with 600 Gb/s across the whole infrastructure targeted by year end. Talks in China on 3 July 2026 covered network expansion, a national data centre, a sovereign cloud, rural connectivity and AI, and are stated to be heading for a comprehensive memorandum and framework agreement that is not yet signed

subject: geopol.eu
name: European co-financed cable connection (MEDUSA)
milestone: Construction and maintenance agreement signed, May 2026
position_end: C&MA signed on a Mediterranean-anchored system

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Gulf-linked digital and statistical engagement
status: Implemented, one memorandum and no implementation on record
milestone: Statistical cooperation protocol signed at Riyadh
position_end: Two instruments, neither a bilateral Gulf digital agreement. In 2019 a memorandum was signed in Conakry between the government and the Arab League's Economic Unity Council for implementation of projects based on the joint Arab vision for the digital economy, and the head of the Arab federation for digital economy was appointed special adviser to the government on digital transformation; the United Arab Emirates is credited with supporting and following up the initiative but is not a signatory, and no implementation is documented. In November 2025 the planning minister signed a protocol with his Saudi counterpart at a United Nations industrial conference to strengthen bilateral cooperation in planning and statistics, training and institutional development; it names no telecommunications, data-centre, cloud, artificial-intelligence or digital-identity deliverable

subject: geopol.india
name: e-VBAB Network Project memorandum with TCIL
status: Implemented, nothing on the record since 2019
milestone: Signed in Conakry 2019-08-02 during the Indian presidential visit
position_start: No India-Guinea digital cooperation agreement, line of credit or programme document held
position_end: One of three memoranda signed in Conakry on 2 August 2019, between Guinea's higher education ministry and Telecommunications Consultants India Limited, for participation in the e-VBAB Network Project — the technology upgrade of India's Pan-African e-Network tele-education and telemedicine satellite platform. It is the only Guinea-specific Indian digital instrument on the record
